parsed_payload.reasoning: Let A=n, B, C. Since the triangle is acute, the foot H of the altitude from C lies on AB, and the circumcenter O lies inside. The angle bisector from B and the altitude segment CH meet inside the triangle, so X also lies inside. Thus O and X are on the same side of BC. Because B,O,X,C are concyclic, the angles subtending chord BC from the same side are equal: ∠BOC=∠BXC. As O is the circumcenter, ∠BOC=2A=2n. In triangle BXC, ∠XBC=B/2. In right triangle BCH, ∠BCH=90°−B, and since C,X,H are collinear, ∠BCX=90°−B. Therefore ∠BXC=180°−B/2−(90°−B)=90°+B/2. Hence 2n=90°+B/2, so B=4n−180. Then C=180°−n−B=360°−5n. For the triangle to be acute, B and C must be positive and less than 90°, giving 54<n<67.5. The largest integer in this interval is 67. At n=67, B=88 and C=25, both acute, and the equal angles ensure the required concyclicity. Thus the largest possible value is \boxed{67}.
